slices.name: Part E — Promote ScriptedProvider + 8 new k3s regression tests

tasks.description:
Create `shared/egg_harness/testing/__init__.py` (exports
`ScriptedProvider`) and `shared/egg_harness/testing/scripted_provider.py`
containing the `ScriptedProvider` class plus its
`_stream_events` helper, copied verbatim from
`shared/tests/test_egg_harness/test_integration.py` (lines
39-43 and 130-163 at HEAD). Keep the existing public
surface identical: constructor takes `script: list[list[StreamEvent]]`;
`name` property returns `"scripted"`; `send_message`
coroutine yields `StreamEvent` objects from the next
scripted entry and records `call_history`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
`python -c "from egg_harness.testing import ScriptedProvider; p = ScriptedProvider([]); assert p.name == 'scripted'; print('ok')"`
prints `ok`. `make lint` passes.

tasks.description:
In `shared/tests/test_egg_harness/test_integration.py`,
replace the inline `class ScriptedProvider:` definition and
its private `_stream_events` helper with re-export shims
from `egg_harness.testing.scripted_provider`. The five
existing call sites (lines 203, 276, 360, 402, 473 at HEAD)
must continue to resolve `ScriptedProvider(script)`
unchanged. The unrelated `RecordingRegistry` class stays
inline.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
`grep -n "^class ScriptedProvider\|^async def _stream_events" shared/tests/test_egg_harness/test_integration.py`
returns no hits. `make test` passes the
`shared/tests/test_egg_harness/test_integration.py` suite.

tasks.description:
Add `shared/tests/test_egg_harness/test_scripted_provider.py`
with two tests: (a) `from egg_harness.testing import
ScriptedProvider` resolves and the class is the same object
imported from `egg_harness.testing.scripted_provider`; (b)
construct `ScriptedProvider([])`, assert `.name ==
"scripted"` and `.call_history == []`.

Create `integration_tests/regression/__init__.py` (empty)
and `integration_tests/regression/conftest.py`. The conftest
re-exports the parent `integration_tests/conftest.py`
fixtures so existing k8s harness fixtures (egg_stack,
kubectl helpers, etc.) are available without rewiring, and
adds three regression-specific helpers used by the 8 new
tests: (a) `start_pipeline(test_request)` that mints a
deterministic pipeline_id from the test nodeid and returns
a started pipeline; (b) `pod_env(pipeline_id, role)` that
shells out to `kubectl get pod -o jsonpath` and returns the
named container's env-var dict; (c) `gateway_audit_log_pushes(pipeline_id, ref)`
that reads the gateway audit log for push events targeting
`ref` and returns the list ordered by timestamp.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
`.venv/bin/pytest --collect-only integration_tests/regression/ -q`
reports 0 errors. The three helpers are importable from
`integration_tests.regression.conftest`. `make lint` passes.

tasks.description:
Add `integration_tests/regression/test_slice_branch_env.py`
covering #2428 (slice-spawn EGG_BRANCH threading). Spin up
a 2-slice DAG pipeline using the conftest's `start_pipeline`
helper; once both slice coders are scheduled, call
`pod_env(pipeline_id, "coder", slice_id=N)` for each slice;
assert each pod's `EGG_BRANCH` value matches its slice's
ref (`egg/<issue>/slice-N/work` or equivalent). Inline
assertion message must reference #2428 so test failures
point at the regression. Mark with `@pytest.mark.integration`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
`.venv/bin/pytest integration_tests/regression/test_slice_branch_env.py -v`
passes on `main`. Reverting #2428's `_compose_branch_env`
fix on a scratch branch causes the test to fail with the
inline #2428 message.

tasks.description:
Add `integration_tests/regression/test_live_pod_guard.py`
covering #2420 (live-pod guard on restart). Start a
pipeline; wait for at least one agent pod to be Running;
call `start_pipeline` again with `force=False`; assert the
response refuses with the live-pod-guard error. Retry with
`force=True`; assert it succeeds and the new pipeline
replaces the old one (different scheduling timestamp on the
new pod set). Mark with `@pytest.mark.integration`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Test passes on `main`. Reverting #2420's guard makes the
second `start_pipeline(force=False)` call succeed and the
test fails on the refusal assertion.

tasks.description:
Add `integration_tests/regression/test_unpushed_commit_salvage.py`
covering #2429 (unpushed-commit salvage). Drive a coder
agent into a state where it tries to push a file under
`docs/` (which is outside coder's gateway-allowed paths) —
this forces a real 403 from the gateway's restricted-path
policy with no mocks (HITL Q2). Assert (a) the push fails,
(b) a recovery branch ref appears on origin before the
worktree is torn down (matching #2429's salvage code path),
(c) the recovery ref points at the unpushed commit SHA.
Mark with `@pytest.mark.integration`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Test passes on `main`. Reverting #2429's salvage code path
causes the recovery-ref-exists assertion to fail with a
message naming #2429.

tasks.description:
Add `integration_tests/regression/test_hitl_round_trip.py`
covering #2430 (HITL alive-signal bypass). Use
`ScriptedProvider` (imported from `egg_harness.testing`) to
drive a refiner that registers an HITL decision via
`register_open_question`. Observe the pipeline transition
to AWAITING_HUMAN. Call `provide_input` resolving the
decision. Assert (a) the pipeline resumes within a bounded
deadline, (b) phase_complete fires for refine, (c) the
downstream plan phase actually starts. Mark with
`@pytest.mark.integration`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Test passes on `main`. Reverting #2430's alive-signal
bypass fix causes the resume-within-deadline assertion to
time out and fail.

tasks.description:
Add `integration_tests/regression/test_brc_single_cycle.py`
covering the BRC happy-path invariant. Drive a single
producer/reviewer phase to completion using
`ScriptedProvider`. Count BRC messages by type using
`mcp__brc__read_peer_artifact` or direct
`egg-orch message list --type CONSENSUS_*` queries. Assert
exactly 1 `CONSENSUS_PROPOSE`, N `CONSENSUS_ACK` (one per
reviewer in the roster), 0 `CONSENSUS_NACK`, and 1
`CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED`. Mark with `@pytest.mark.integration`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Test passes on `main`. If a future change makes the
producer emit two PROPOSE messages, the exact-count
assertion fires.

tasks.description:
Add `integration_tests/regression/test_slice_dag_restart.py`
covering test E.6 (decision-4). Spin up a 3-slice DAG
pipeline. Wait until slice-2's coder reaches PROPOSE state
(observe via the `CONSENSUS_PROPOSE` message from
slice-2's coder role). Record slice-2's branch ref commit
SHA via `git ls-remote origin egg/<issue>/slice-2/work` or
equivalent. Call `restart_agent` on slice-2's coder. Wait
for the agent to recover. Assert (a) slice-2's branch ref
commit SHA is unchanged across the restart, (b) the
pipeline eventually reaches `PR_READY`. Mark with
`@pytest.mark.integration`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Test passes on `main`. Reverting #2535's
slice-N-doesn't-inherit-slice-(N-1)-consensus invariant
(or any future regression that changes slice-2's ref on
restart) trips the unchanged-SHA assertion. Deterministic
checkpoints — no wall-clock sleeps.

tasks.description:
Add `integration_tests/regression/test_phase_aware_timeout.py`
covering test E.7 (HITL Q3). Configure
`consensus_timeout_minutes_plan = 1` via the contract /
orchestrator phase_configs API. Have the plan-phase
planner role not emit any CONSENSUS_PROPOSE (use a
ScriptedProvider that returns silent turns). Assert
`CONSENSUS_TIMEOUT` event fires within 60±10s of plan
phase start. Docstring must note the issue text's
`consensus_timeout_s = 30` was a typo — the real field is
`consensus_timeout_minutes_<phase>`. Mark with
`@pytest.mark.integration`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Test passes on `main`. Setting the timeout to 10 minutes
on a scratch branch causes the within-60±10s assertion to
fail.

tasks.description:
Add `integration_tests/regression/test_babysit_pr_single_push.py`
covering test E.8 (HITL Q4). Drive a babysit-PR run through
2 coder revisions using ScriptedProvider trajectories. After
BRC reaches CONFIRMED, query the **gateway audit log of
push events** (via `gateway_audit_log_pushes` from
conftest, HITL Q4 — authoritative source) for pushes
targeting the PR head ref. Assert exactly 1 successful
push to the PR head ref across the full babysit-PR run.
Mark with `@pytest.mark.integration`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Test passes on `main`. Reverting
`_babysit_final_push_head_move_guard` (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py)
causes a second push to land on the head ref and the
exact-count assertion fires.

tasks.description:

decisions.question: How should the remaining work (Parts A, E, F) be packaged into PRs?

options.label: One PR containing A+E+F together (single review, atomic delivery)
Two PRs: E (ScriptedProvider + new tests) first, then A+F together (wire gate once tests proven green)
Three sequential PRs: E → A → F (smallest reviewable chunks, tightest bisect)
Two PRs: A+F (wiring + docs) first as advisory, then E (expansion) follow-up
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Other (explain in reply): Three slices = three PRs. slice-1 = Part E (ScriptedProvider promotion + 8 new tests under integration_tests/regression/). slice-2 = Part A (wire test-integration.yml into test.yml as a new 'integration' job). slice-3 = Part F (CLAUDE.md + docs/guides/testing.md updates), depends on slice-1 because F's docs reference the regression subdir E creates. slice-1 and slice-2 run in parallel; slice-3 follows slice-1. The canned 'Three sequential PRs' option is wrong because slices can run in parallel — this is a slice-DAG with one dependency edge, not a serial chain. Plan phase MUST produce a 3-slice DAG and NOT a single-slice plan with multiple PRs. The refiner registered this decision as a 'PR count' question rather than a slice-DAG question; tracking issue for that framing confusion: #2584."}

Inside .github/workflows/on-pull-request.yml as a separate workflow_call alongside the existing code review
A new top-level workflow file dedicated to integration tests with its own pull_request trigger
Inline pull_request trigger added directly to test-integration.yml (no wrapper)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Inside .github/workflows/test.yml as a new `integration` job sibling of `unit` and `security`, included in the existing aggregate"}

decisions.question: What gating policy should the new integration check use at merge time?

options.label: Non-blocking from day 1; flip to required-for-merge after observed stability across ~10 PRs (matches issue text recommendation)

decisions.question: [Phase gate: refine] The refine phase has completed. Please review the analysis and approve to continue, or provide feedback to request changes.

options.label: approve
request changes

decisions.resolution:
## Resolved Questions

**decision-1 (PR/slice packaging)**: Three slices = three PRs. slice-1 = Part E (ScriptedProvider promotion + 8 new tests under integration_tests/regression/). slice-2 = Part A (wire test-integration.yml into test.yml as new 'integration' job). slice-3 = Part F (CLAUDE.md + docs/guides/testing.md). Soft dep: slice-3 depends on slice-1 (F's docs reference the regression subdir E creates). slice-1 and slice-2 can run in parallel. NOTE: The refiner registered this as a 'PR count' decision; the operator clarified it should be framed in slice-DAG terms. Plan phase must produce a 3-slice DAG, not a single-slice plan with multiple PRs. Tracking issue for the refiner's framing confusion: #2584.

**decision-2 (where workflow_call lives)**: Inside .github/workflows/test.yml as a new 'integration' job sibling to 'unit' and 'security', included in the existing 'aggregate'. This keeps 'Test / aggregate' as the canonical required-check name (slice-2 implementation detail).

**decision-3 (gating policy)**: Required-for-merge from day 1. NOT the issue text's recommended non-blocking-with-settle-in approach. Operator chose tighter gating; flake risk is accepted.

**decision-4 (E.6 scenario)**: 3-slice DAG; restart slice-2's coder while it is in PROPOSE; assert slice-2's branch ref commit SHA is unchanged across the restart and the pipeline reaches PR_READY.

**decision-5 (wall-clock budget)**: No fixed budget. Existing test-integration.yml runtime (~10-15 min after Part E adds) is acceptable. Flag in a follow-up if PR latency becomes a complaint; no shard plan needed yet.

**decision-6 (test-all inclusion)**: Stay unit-only. `make test-integration` remains a separate explicit target. Do not fold integration tier into `make test-all`.

**decision-7 (TestCredentialIsolation gap)**: Out-of-scope for #2474. Tracked in follow-up issue #2585.

**Q1 (flake guards)**: Defend against image-import flakes (retry), kubectl wait timeouts (explicit deadlines), and on-failure capture (`kubectl get events --all-namespaces` + pod logs as workflow artifact). Standard k3s harness hardening set.

**Q2 (E.3 push-rejection mechanism)**: Coder role pushes a docs file to force a real 403 from the gateway's restricted-path policy. Exercises the real code path; no mocks.

**Q3 (E.7 timeout granularity)**: Use minute-granular timing. Configure `consensus_timeout_minutes_plan = 1`; observe CONSENSUS_TIMEOUT event fires within 60±10s. Do NOT add second-granular config support in this pipeline — the existing minutes-based API is sufficient for the assertion. Update the test's docstring to note the issue text's `consensus_timeout_s = 30` was a typo (the real field is `consensus_timeout_minutes_<phase>`).

**Q4 (E.8 push-counting method)**: Gateway audit log of push events. Authoritative source; counts every push attempt and outcome.

**Q5 (required-flip SLO)**: N/A — operator chose Required-from-day-1 for decision-3, so the non-blocking → required transition does not exist.

**Q6 (CLAUDE.md naming)**: Generic note pointing at integration_tests/regression/. No specific test files named — keeps the docs low-maintenance.

## Scope Expansion (operator pre-refine instruction)

When a new regression test fails against current `main`, the pipeline MUST diagnose the production-code root cause and fix it in the relevant slice's PR — these tests are designed to catch real regressions; closing those gaps is in scope. When a new test is itself broken or flaky, fix the test rather than skipping or marking xfail.

## Plan-Phase Instructions

- Produce a 3-slice DAG: slice-1 (E), slice-2 (A), slice-3 (F). slice-3 has dep on slice-1.
- slice-1 owns: ScriptedProvider promotion to shared/egg_harness/testing/scripted_provider.py (+ shared/egg_harness/testing/__init__.py); 8 new tests in integration_tests/regression/ with shared conftest; minutes-based assertion in E.7; gateway-audit-log assertion in E.8; coder-pushes-docs-file mechanism for E.3; 3-slice/restart-slice-2-in-PROPOSE scenario for E.6.
- slice-2 owns: workflow_call invocation in test.yml under a new 'integration' job, included in 'aggregate'; flake guards (image-import retry, kubectl wait timeouts, on-failure kubectl-events artifact); PR description must document the exact required-check name to flip in repo Settings → Branch protection.
- slice-3 owns: Quick-Reference bullet in CLAUDE.md (`make test-integration  # Cross-module regressions; requires k3s (see docs/guides/testing.md)`); short Integration-tests subsection in CLAUDE.md after 'Key Entry Points' (generic, no named test files); top-level Integration-tests section in docs/guides/testing.md (k3s-only setup recipe, required-check name, CI gating notes).
- Each slice's failing tests against `main` (if any) trigger production-code fixes in that slice's PR per the scope expansion above.

No specific past flakes called out beyond the standard set.", "Q2": "Coder role pushes a docs file (e.g. a path under `docs/`) to force a real 403 from the gateway's restricted-path policy. pr.title: Wire integration tests into PR CI; expand coverage (#2474)
pr.description:
The `test-integration.yml` reusable workflow exists and is solid
(k3s + mocked LLMs, exercises gateway/container/network/policy
boundaries), but no PR workflow invokes it — so PRs merge to
`main` without integration tests running. Recent in-process
state-mutation regressions (#2428 slice-spawn env threading,
#2429 unpushed-commit salvage, #2420 live-pod guard on restart,
#2430 HITL alive-signal bypass) all merged through CI green
because the integration tier had no PR gate AND no scenarios
exercising those code paths.

This issue ships the remaining post-#2556 work as a 3-slice
stacked-PR train:

1. **slice-1 (Part E) — Test infrastructure + 8 new regressions.**
   Promotes `ScriptedProvider` from `shared/tests/test_egg_harness/test_integration.py`
   to a public testing API at `shared/egg_harness/testing/scripted_provider.py`,
   then adds 8 new k3s regression tests under
   `integration_tests/regression/` covering #2428, #2429, #2420,
   #2430, BRC single-cycle consensus, slice-DAG mid-flight
   restart, phase-aware consensus timeouts (minute-granular),
   and babysit-PR single-final-push (gateway-audit-log
   assertion).
2. **slice-2 (Part A) — Wire integration tests into PR CI.**
   Stages new `.github-staging/workflows/test.yml` and
   `.github-staging/workflows/test-integration.yml` — coder is
   blocked from `.github/`, so the human reviewer performs the
   `git mv` before merge. Adds an `integration:` job sibling to
   `unit:` and `security:`, included in `aggregate:` so the
   canonical required-check name stays `Test / aggregate`.
   Hardens `test-integration.yml` with image-import retry,
   explicit `kubectl wait` timeouts, and an on-failure
   `k3s-debug` artifact. Required-for-merge from day 1
   (operator-chosen, no settle-in window).
3. **slice-3 (Part F) — Document the integration tier.**
   Adds a `make test-integration` Quick-Reference bullet and a
   short "Integration tests" subsection in `CLAUDE.md` after
   "Key Entry Points"; adds a top-level "Integration tests"
   section in `docs/guides/testing.md` with the k3s-only setup
   recipe, required-check name, and CI gating notes. Generic
   references only — no specific test filenames called out.

slice-1 and slice-2 are independent roots and run in parallel.
slice-3 stacks on slice-1 because its docs reference the
`integration_tests/regression/` directory slice-1 creates.

Net effect after the stack merges: every PR runs the integration
tier, the canonical `Test / aggregate` check covers it, and
agents have a documented entry point for adding cross-module /
state-machine regression coverage.
pr.test_plan:
- Automated:
  * `make lint` — passes on every slice via the existing `Lint` workflow.
  * `make test-all` — unit suite stays green on every slice; new tests in `integration_tests/regression/` are NOT collected here (testpaths exclude).
  * `make test-integration` — passes locally on k3s after slice-1; passes in CI on every PR once slice-2 lands.
  * New unit test `shared/tests/test_egg_harness/test_scripted_provider.py` guards the promoted public API.
  * Each of the 8 new regression tests in slice-1 includes an inline reversion check — reverting the production fix it covers makes the test fail with a clear assertion. Verified by manually reverting each fix on a scratch branch.
- Manual:
  * After slice-1 merges: optional `workflow_dispatch` of `test-integration.yml` against slice-1's branch to confirm CI green ahead of slice-2's wiring.
  * After slice-2 merges: confirm `Test / integration` appears on a sample PR and `Test / aggregate` depends on it.
  * After slice-2 merges: repo admin flips `Test / aggregate` to required-for-merge in Settings → Branch protection.
  * After slice-3 merges: a contributor follows the new `docs/guides/testing.md` k3s-on-host recipe on a fresh laptop / Linux VM and reaches `make test-integration` green.
pr.manual_steps:
Pre-merge (slice-2): trigger `test-integration.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` against slice-2's branch; confirm green before merging (the check becomes required-from-day-1 on merge, so a red first run blocks all PRs).
Pre-merge (slice-2): human reviewer runs `git mv .github-staging/workflows/test.yml .github/workflows/test.yml` and `git mv .github-staging/workflows/test-integration.yml .github/workflows/test-integration.yml`, commits, and pushes to slice-2's branch before merge. (coder cannot write under .github/; orchestrator surfaces this as a Pre-merge Obligation on slice-2's PR body.)
Post-merge (slice-2): repo admin flips `Test / aggregate` to required-for-merge in Settings → Branch protection. Required-from-day-1 per decision-3.

questions.question: Flake guards: which sources of CI flake should we pre-emptively defend against in the workflow (image-import retry, kubectl wait timeouts, explicit cleanup on failure with kubectl-events artifact)? Any past CI flake you've observed that should be specifically pinned down?
questions.answer: Image-import retry + kubectl wait timeouts + on-failure kubectl-events artifact. Standard k3s harness hardening: retry on image-import failures (2-3 attempts), set explicit deadlines on every kubectl wait call, capture `kubectl get events --all-namespaces -o yaml` plus pod logs as a workflow artifact on failure. No specific past flakes called out beyond the standard set.

questions.question: Test E.3 (unpushed-commit salvage, #2429): the issue text says 'inject gateway push rejection (use existing restricted-path code path)'. Concretely — should the test push a docs file from the coder role to force a real 403, or is there a different restricted-path code path you'd prefer?
questions.answer: Coder role pushes a docs file (e.g. a path under `docs/`) to force a real 403 from the gateway's restricted-path policy. Exercises the real code path with no mocks. Implement-phase coder may pick the exact path based on the gateway's current policy table.

questions.question: Test E.7 (phase-aware consensus timeouts): the issue says 'configure phase_configs.plan.consensus_timeout_s = 30; assert CONSENSUS_TIMEOUT event fires within 30±5s'. The orchestrator's resolve_consensus_timeout_minutes uses MINUTES, not seconds. Should the test use minute-granular timing (e.g. 1-minute plan timeout, observe 60±10s) or do we need to add second-granular config support first?
questions.answer: Use minute-granular timing. Configure `consensus_timeout_minutes_plan = 1`; assert CONSENSUS_TIMEOUT event fires within 60±10s. Do NOT add second-granular config support in this pipeline — the existing minutes-based API is sufficient for the assertion. Test docstring should note the issue text's `consensus_timeout_s = 30` was a typo (the real field is `consensus_timeout_minutes_<phase>`).

questions.question: Test E.8 (Babysit-PR single final push): the issue mentions `_babysit_final_push_head_move_guard` at orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py — should the test assert via the gateway audit log of push events, or via observing git ls-remote on the PR head ref before/after each coder revision?
questions.answer: Gateway audit log of push events. Authoritative source; counts every push attempt and outcome. `git ls-remote` would miss pushes that didn't move the ref.

questions.question: Once the new check is wired (non-blocking initially), what's the trigger for flipping required-for-merge? '10 PRs without flake' is mentioned in the issue — should this be a defined SLO (e.g. <1 flake per 20 runs measured over 2 weeks), or just maintainer's judgment?
questions.answer: N/A — operator chose Required-for-merge from day 1 for decision-4 (gating policy), so the non-blocking → required transition does not exist. If flake budget becomes an issue post-merge, the question can be revisited as a config rollback.

questions.question: Should Part F's `CLAUDE.md` text mention by name the specific tests added in Part E so future agents can locate them when they need similar coverage (e.g. 'use integration_tests/regression/test_slice_branch_env.py as the template for slice-spawn env-threading regressions'), or keep the note generic to avoid stale references?
questions.answer: Generic note pointing at `integration_tests/regression/`. No specific test files named — keeps the docs low-maintenance and avoids stale references if files are renamed in future work.
